findings.message: nested quantifiers: (…)+ repeats a group that already repeats [0123456789AB]+ — backtracking can be exponential
findings.suggestion: Avoid applying an unbounded quantifier to a group that itself repeats. Reduce to a single quantifier, bound the inner repetition ({1,100}), or use an atomic group / possessive quantifier where the engine supports it.

findings.message: overlapping alternation branches "'a'" and "'a''a'" inside a repeated group (first characters overlap): ambiguous matching can backtrack exponentially
findings.suggestion: Make the branches unambiguous (e.g. `(a|aa)` -> `a+` if equivalent, or order branches longest-first and use an atomic/possessive group), or replace the alternation with a character class if the branches are single characters.

findings.message: backreference \1 appears inside a repeated group: backtracking engines can exhibit exponential behaviour matching backreferences
findings.suggestion: Avoid repeating a group that contains a backreference, or bound the repetition and anchor the pattern.
